title: Communication in the context of a project
apm_learning_objective: Understand communication in the context of a project.
exam_coverage_note: 5 of 60 marks. Note that advantages and disadvantages of communication methods are two separate outcomes, so the methods are worth two marks between them.
source_ref: APM PFQ Qualification Handbook, APM-QS-PFQ-8 V5 (April 2026), §11d. Syllabus maps this objective to APM Body of Knowledge 7th ed. 3.3.1 and 8th ed. 4.1.4.
competence_area_note: The handbook publishes no per-objective Competence Framework mapping. Left null rather than guessed.
where_this_fits: Five marks, and easier than it looks once you notice one thing: two of the outcomes ask for the advantages and then the disadvantages of the same three communication methods. Learning face to face, physical and virtual properly is the best return in the objective.

key_definitions.definition: The exchange of information between parties, and the confirmation that a shared understanding has been reached.
key_definitions.plain_english: Not just sending something. Making sure it landed the way you meant it.

key_definitions.definition: Communication conducted in person, allowing verbal and non-verbal signals to be exchanged directly.
key_definitions.plain_english: In the same room, reading the body language as well as the words.

key_definitions.definition: Communication through tangible written or printed material, such as reports, letters and documents.
key_definitions.plain_english: Something written down that exists as a record.

key_definitions.definition: Communication mediated by technology, such as video calls, email, messaging and collaboration tools.
key_definitions.plain_english: Anything that needs a network and a device to happen.

key_definitions.definition: A document setting out what information will be communicated to whom, when, how, and by whom.
key_definitions.plain_english: Who hears what, how often, in what form, and whose job it is to send it.

core_content.key_takeaway: Communication is the exchange of information between parties, together with confirmation that a shared understanding has been reached. The second half is the part people drop. Sending information is transmission, and it only becomes communication once it has been received and understood as intended.
core_content.body_markdown:
Sending information is transmission. A report nobody opened has been distributed, not communicated.

The word exchange matters too. Communication runs in both directions. A project manager who issues weekly reports and receives nothing back has a broadcast, and broadcasts are how projects find out late that a stakeholder has been quietly unhappy for two months.

This is why confirmation is in the definition. Asking someone to say back what they have understood, or noticing that their questions imply a different picture, is what closes the loop.

Communication also covers more than status information. It includes building relationships, managing expectations and reaching agreement.

core_content.outcome_title: Outline the advantages of different communication methods
core_content.key_takeaway: Face to face lets non-verbal signals be seen and gives immediate feedback, so it is the strongest method for building trust and for anything sensitive. Physical communication, meaning written or printed material, produces a durable and accurate record that everyone receives in identical form and can read at their own pace. Virtual communication reaches people wherever they are, is fast and cheap compared with travel, can reach many at once, and usually leaves a searchable trail.
core_content.body_markdown:
Each method has its own advantages and the exam expects you to attach the right one to the right method.

Face to face carries tone, expression and hesitation, which say things words alone do not. Misunderstandings can be corrected on the spot.

Physical communication conveys complex detail precisely, and the recipient can return to it later.

Virtual communication makes dispersed and international teams workable.

A good communication plan uses all three, matched to the message rather than to habit.

core_content.outcome_title: Outline the disadvantages of different communication methods
core_content.key_takeaway: Face to face needs people in the same place at the same time, costs time and money, normally leaves no record unless someone takes one, and does not scale. Physical communication is slow, gives no immediate feedback, carries no tone, and is largely one way. Virtual communication depends on technology being available and reliable, loses non-verbal signal so conflict is harder to spot, and the ease of copying people in creates noise that hides the signal.
core_content.body_markdown:
The same three methods, and a separate mark for their weaknesses.

Face to face is often impossible for a dispersed team, and because it usually leaves no record, what was agreed can be disputed afterwards.

Physical communication carries no tone, which makes it easy to read a neutral message as curt. Volume becomes its own problem, because when there is too much of it people stop reading.

Virtual communication makes conflict and disengagement harder to detect, and time zones complicate scheduling.

The general principle is that every method trades something. Richness against reach, speed against permanence, immediacy against record.

core_content.outcome_title: Outline the contents of a communication plan
core_content.key_takeaway: A communication plan records the stakeholders or audiences, what information each one needs and why, the frequency or timing, the method or channel, who is responsible for producing and sending it, and any feedback mechanism. It follows from stakeholder analysis, which identifies who matters, and it is a live document that changes as the project moves through its phases.
core_content.body_markdown:
The plan records the decisions about project communication so that it happens deliberately rather than reactively.

It follows from analysis. Stakeholder analysis identifies who matters and how much influence they hold. The communication plan turns that into a schedule of specific actions. Without the analysis the plan is guesswork, and without the plan the analysis changes nothing.

It is a live document. Stakeholders change as the project moves through its phases, and their information needs change with them. A plan written once and never revisited ends up describing an audience that has moved on.

core_content.outcome_title: Explain the benefits, to a project manager, of a communication plan
core_content.key_takeaway: A communication plan makes communication deliberate rather than reactive, so the right people get the right information at the right time instead of whoever asks loudest. It manages expectations, targets the project manager's limited time where communication changes the outcome, keeps the message consistent, and gives each communication a named owner. What it cannot do is make people agree.
core_content.body_markdown:
The outcome asks for the benefits from the project manager's point of view, so learn them in that form.

Without a plan, communication defaults to whoever asks loudest. The stakeholders who chase get information, and the ones who do not, who may matter more, are neglected until they become a problem.

People who are told what is happening on a predictable schedule are much less likely to invent their own version of events in the gaps.

Consistency matters most when the news is bad. Everyone hearing the same message beats several versions circulating.

And naming who sends what, and when, means communication has an owner rather than being everybody's job and therefore nobody's.

misconceptions.wrong: If the report was sent, it was communicated.
misconceptions.right: Communication requires the information to be received and understood. Sending is transmission. Confirmation of shared understanding is what completes it.

misconceptions.wrong: Face to face is always the best method.
misconceptions.right: It is the richest, and it is expensive, unscalable and leaves no record. The correct method depends on the message, the audience and the need for a record.

misconceptions.wrong: Virtual communication leaves no audit trail.
misconceptions.right: Most forms leave a searchable one. The genuine disadvantages are technology dependence and reduced non-verbal signal.

misconceptions.wrong: Written communication is the safest because it cannot be misunderstood.
misconceptions.right: It carries no tone and offers no immediate feedback, so misunderstandings persist longer precisely because nobody notices them.

misconceptions.wrong: A communication plan is a list of meetings.
misconceptions.right: It records who receives what information, when, how, and who is responsible for it. Meetings are one channel among several.

misconceptions.wrong: A good communication plan keeps stakeholders happy.
misconceptions.right: It ensures the right information reaches the right people at the right time. Some of them will still disagree, and a plan that hides that is failing.

memory_aids.acronym: Who, what, when, how, by whom
memory_aids.expansion: The five questions a communication plan answers. If an option does not answer one of them, it is not plan content.
Face to face is rich, virtual has reach, physical leaves a record. Three methods, three strengths, and the disadvantage of each is usually the absence of the other two.
The confirmation half of the definition. Any option stopping at distribution is incomplete.

progress_checkpoint: I can define communication including the confirmation of shared understanding.
I can name the three communication methods in the syllabus.
I can give two advantages of each method, attached to the right one.
I can give two disadvantages of each method, attached to the right one.
I can list the contents of a communication plan and name two things that do not belong in it.
I can give four benefits of a communication plan and explain why it cannot guarantee stakeholder agreement.

source_confidence.claim: The three communication methods named in the syllabus are face to face, physical and virtual.
source_confidence.basis: Named in the bracketed 'including' lists in syllabus outcomes 9.2 and 9.3. The handbook states bracketed content is examinable.

source_confidence.claim: Advantages and disadvantages are separate learning outcomes, worth a mark each.
source_confidence.basis: PFQ Handbook §11d lists them as two distinct outcomes; §12c states one question per outcome.
source_confidence.risk: None material. Candidates who revise the methods once, in one direction, are preparing for one of the two marks.
